::: {#exr-fewest-roads}
#### The fewest roads

Seven towns, $a$ to $g$, lie in a valley, with $g$ in the middle.
@fig-hub draws the nine roads that could be built between them.
The county wants to build as few of these roads as it can,
so that people can drive between every two towns.
How many roads must it build?

::: {#fig-hub}

Six of them, a, b, c, d, e and f, sit at the corners of a hexagon in that order, each joined to the next, and f joined back to a.
